Market intelligence reports indicate that the memory cost Apple pays for the iPhone 18 Pro will be four times that of last year's model.

TrendForce says Apple will not pass all of the cost on to consumers, and will rely more on services revenue to offset the pressure of rising hardware manufacturing costs⋯⋯

Apple announced significant price increases for most of its products back in June, saying at the time that it had exhausted every possible way to delay, but had no other choice.

Apple did not raise the prices of existing iPhones at the time, but this situation is expected to change next week. TrendForce points out that the sharp rise in memory costs for the new models is the main reason.

Apple is not expected to pass on the full increase in memory costs in iPhone pricing. The market currently estimates that the iPhone 18 Pro will be priced around USD 100 higher than the iPhone 17 Pro.

This is because a sharp price hike would cause even the most loyal Apple fans to upgrade less frequently. TrendForce says Apple will not want to sacrifice its continued growth, and also notes that the weak macroeconomic environment is making consumers more cautious with their spending.

The company forecasts that Apple's first foldable phone, the iPhone Ultra, could start at $2,299, with top configurations exceeding $3,000.
